newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says U.S. economy "on solid footing".
newsitem.headline: Rubin says U.S. economy "on solid footing".

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Friday said that the U.S. economy is "on solid footing" with good growth and inflation under control.

Speaking to reporters following testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on a proposed balanced budget amendment, Rubin said the administration would do all it could to defeat the proposed amendment on the grounds that it would hurt the U.S. economy.

Asked about his position on capital gains tax cut proposals circulating in Congress, Rubin said the administration has its own tax proposals and "they'll not surprise you. They'll continue to be middle-income tax cuts of the kind the president has spoken about. We do not have a broad-based capital gains tax as one of our priorities," he said.

Asked about replacement for two openings in the Federal Reserve Board, Rubin told reporters that the administratrion had begun "a process" to find them and that choices would be made "as expeditiously as possible."
